title.zh: 卷一百四十三 列傳第六十八 高元李韋薛崔戴王徐郗辛
title.en: Volume 143 Biographies 68: Gao, Yuan, Li, Wei, Xue, Cui, Dai, Wang, Xu, Chi, Xin
title.raw: 卷一百四十三 列傳第六十八 高元李韋薛崔戴王徐郗辛 Volume 143 Biographies 68: Gao, Yuan, Li, Wei, Xue, Cui, Dai, Wang, Xu, Chi, Xin

sentences.zh: 高元李韋薛崔戴王徐郗辛

translations.literal: Gao, Yuan, Li, Wei, Xue, Cui, Dai, Wang, Xu, Xi, Xin
translations.idiomatic: Gao, Yuan, Li, Wei, Xue, Cui, Dai, Wang, Xu, Xi, and Xin

sentences.zh: 高適，字達夫，滄州渤海人。

translations.literal: Gao Shi, styled Dafu, was a man of Bohai in Cang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Shi, courtesy name Dafu, was a native of Bohai in Cang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 少落魄，不治生事。

translations.literal: In youth he lived in obscurity and did not attend to the business of making a living.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he lived in obscurity and gave no thought to earning a livelihood.

sentences.zh: 客梁、宋間，宋州刺史張九臯奇之，舉有道科中第，調封丘尉，不得誌，去。

translations.literal: He traveled as a guest in the regions of Liang and Song. Zhang Jiugao, prefect of Song Prefecture, admired him, recommended him for the daoyue examination, on which he passed, and he was appointed assistant magistrate of Fengqiu—but his ambition was not fulfilled, so he left.
translations.idiomatic: While traveling as a guest in the Liang and Song region, Zhang Jiugao, prefect of Song Prefecture, took notice of him and recommended him for the daoyue examination, which he passed. He was then assigned as assistant magistrate of Fengqiu, but when his ambitions were not realized, he resigned and left.

sentences.zh: 客河西，河西節度使哥舒翰表為左驍衛兵曹參軍，掌書記。

translations.literal: He traveled west of the Yellow River. Geshu Han, military commissioner of Hexi, memorialized the throne to appoint him Left Xiaoqi Corps Army Staff Assistant, in charge of secretarial duties.
translations.idiomatic: He then traveled to the region west of the Yellow River, where Geshu Han, military commissioner of Hexi, recommended him for appointment as Left Xiaoqi Corps Army Staff Assistant with responsibility for secretarial work.

sentences.zh: 祿山亂，召翰討賊，即拜適左拾遺，轉監察御史，佐翰守潼關。

translations.literal: When An Lushan rebelled, [the emperor] summoned Geshu Han to suppress the rebels and at once appointed Gao Shi Left Reminder, then transferred him to Censor, assisting Han in defending Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan rose in rebellion, the emperor summoned Geshu Han to suppress the rebels and immediately appointed Gao Shi Left Reminder, then transferred him to Censor to assist Han in defending Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 翰敗，帝問群臣策安出，適請竭禁藏募死士抗賊，未為晚，不省。

translations.literal: When Han was defeated, the emperor asked the assembled ministers what plan should be adopted. Gao Shi urged that the private treasury be exhausted to recruit desperate warriors to resist the rebels—it was not yet too late—but the emperor took no notice.
translations.idiomatic: After Han's defeat, the emperor asked his ministers what course to take. Gao Shi urged that the imperial treasury be emptied to recruit desperate men to resist the rebels, arguing that it was not yet too late—but the emperor paid no heed.

sentences.zh: 天子西幸，適走間道及帝於河池，因言：「翰忠義有素，而病奪其明，乃至荒踣。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven fled west. Gao Shi traveled by a secret route and caught up with the emperor at Hechi, where he said: "Han has always been loyal and righteous, but illness robbed him of clear judgment, and so he came to this disastrous fall.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor fled west, Gao Shi took a bypath and caught up with him at Hechi. There he said: "Han has always been loyal and righteous, but illness clouded his judgment, and so he came to this ruinous defeat.

sentences.zh: 監軍諸將不恤軍務，以倡優蒲飗相娛樂，渾、隴武士飯糲米日不厭，而責死戰，其敗固宜。

translations.literal: The supervising eunuchs and generals paid no heed to military affairs, amusing one another with actors and frivolous entertainments. The warriors of Hun and Long ate coarse rice day after day without complaint, yet were required to fight to the death—their defeat was only to be expected.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch supervisors and generals neglected military affairs, diverting themselves with actors and idle amusements. The soldiers of Hun and Long ate coarse rice every day without complaint, yet were ordered to fight to the death—their defeat was inevitable.

sentences.zh: 又魯炅、何履光、趙國珍屯南陽，而一二中人監軍更用事，是能取勝哉？

translations.literal: Moreover, Lu Hui, He Luguang, and Zhao Guozhen were encamped at Nanyang, while one or two eunuch supervisors held power over them—how could such a force hope to win?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Lu Hui, He Luguang, and Zhao Guozhen were stationed at Nanyang, while one or two eunuch supervisors held real authority over them—how could such an army hope to prevail?

sentences.zh: 臣數為楊國忠言之，不肯聽。

translations.literal: Your servant pleaded this many times to Yang Guozhong, but he would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: I raised this with Yang Guozhong again and again, but he refused to listen.

sentences.zh: 故陛下有今日行，未足深恥。」

translations.literal: Therefore Your Majesty's journey today is not in itself deeply shameful.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore Your Majesty's flight today is not in itself a matter of deep shame.

sentences.zh: 帝頷之。

translations.literal: The emperor nodded in assent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor nodded in agreement.

sentences.zh: 俄遷侍御史，擢諫議大夫，負氣敢言，權近側目。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Attending Censor and promoted to Remonstrating Grand Master. He was proud-spirited and daring in speech, and those in power nearby looked upon him askance.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was transferred to Attending Censor and promoted to Remonstrating Grand Master. Proud and outspoken, he drew wary glances from those in power around him.

sentences.zh: 帝以諸王分鎮，適盛言不可，俄而永王叛。

translations.literal: When the emperor assigned the imperial princes to separate regional commands, Gao Shi vigorously argued that this should not be done; soon afterward the Prince of Yong rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor assigned the imperial princes to separate regional commands, Gao Shi strongly argued against it; soon afterward the Prince of Yong rebelled.

sentences.zh: 肅宗雅聞之，召與計事，因判言王且敗，不足憂。

translations.literal: Emperor Suzong had long heard of his reputation and summoned him to discuss affairs. He thereupon declared that the prince would soon be defeated and there was no cause for alarm.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Suzong had long heard of his reputation and summoned him to discuss strategy. Gao Shi declared that the prince would soon be defeated and there was no cause for concern.

sentences.zh: 帝奇之，除揚州大都督府長史、淮南節度使。

translations.literal: The emperor marveled at this and appointed him Senior Administrator of the Yangzhou Military Governorship and Military Commissioner of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was impressed and appointed him Senior Administrator of the Yangzhou Military Governorship and Military Commissioner of Huainan.

sentences.zh: 詔與江東韋陟、淮西來瑱率師會安陸，方濟師而王敗。

translations.literal: An edict ordered him to join forces with Wei Zhi of Jiangdong and Lai Tian of Huaixi and lead troops to assemble at Anlu. Just as he was about to cross the river with his army, the prince was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered him to join Wei Zhi of Jiangdong and Lai Tian of Huaixi in leading troops to assemble at Anlu. Just as he was about to ferry his army across, the prince was defeated.

sentences.zh: 李輔國惡其才，數短毀之，下除太子少詹事。

translations.literal: Li Fuguo resented his talent and repeatedly slandered him, resulting in his demotion to Junior Mentor of the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: Li Fuguo resented his ability and repeatedly slandered him, and he was demoted to Junior Mentor of the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 未幾蜀亂，出為蜀、彭二州刺史。

translations.literal: Before long there was disorder in Shu, and he was sent out to serve as prefect of the two prefectures of Shu and Peng.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, when disorder broke out in Shu, he was sent out to serve as prefect of Shu and Peng.

sentences.zh: 始，上皇東還，分劍南為兩節度，百姓弊於調度，而西山三城列戍。

translations.literal: At the beginning, when the Retired Emperor returned east, Jiannan was divided into two military circuits. The people were worn down by levies and requisitions, while three walled cities in the western mountains were garrisoned in a line.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the Retired Emperor returned east, Jiannan was split into two military circuits. The people were exhausted by levies and requisitions, while three fortified cities in the western mountains were garrisoned in succession.

sentences.zh: 適上疏曰：「劍南雖名東、西川，其實一道。

translations.literal: Gao Shi submitted a memorial saying: "Although Jiannan is called Eastern and Western Chuan, in fact it is a single circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Shi submitted a memorial stating: "Although Jiannan is called Eastern and Western Chuan, it is in fact one circuit.

sentences.zh: 自邛關、黎、雅以抵南蠻，由茂而西，經羌中、平戎等城，界吐蕃。

translations.literal: From Qiong Pass, Li, and Ya to the southern barbarians, and west from Mao through the cities of Qiangzhong, Pingrong, and others, it borders Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: From Qiong Pass, Li, and Ya down to the southern tribes, and west from Mao through Qiangzhong, Pingrong, and other cities, it borders Tibet.

sentences.zh: 瀕邊諸城，皆仰給劍南。

translations.literal: All the border cities depend on Jiannan for their supplies.
translations.idiomatic: All the frontier cities rely on Jiannan for their provisions.

sentences.zh: 異時以全蜀之饒，而山南佐之，猶不能舉，今裂梓、遂等八州專為一節度，歲月之計，西川不得參也。

translations.literal: In former times, even with the full wealth of Shu supplemented by Shannan, [the burden] still could not be borne. Now Zi, Sui, and seven other prefectures have been carved off into a separate circuit, and in the monthly accounting Western Chuan has no share in it.
translations.idiomatic: In the past, even with all the wealth of Shu supplemented by Shannan, the burden could scarcely be met. Now Zi, Sui, and seven other prefectures have been carved off into a separate circuit, and in the monthly accounting Western Chuan has no part in it.

sentences.zh: 嘉陵比困夷獠，日雖小定，而痍痏未平，耕紡亡業，衣食貿易皆資成都，是不可得役亦明矣。

translations.literal: Jialing has lately been troubled by Yi and Liao tribesmen. Though the region has been somewhat pacified day by day, wounds are not yet healed, farming and weaving have been abandoned, and food, clothing, and trade all depend on Chengdu—it is clear that [these people] cannot be conscripted for labor.
translations.idiomatic: Jialing has lately been harried by Yi and Liao tribesmen. Though the region has been somewhat pacified, its wounds are not yet healed, farming and weaving have been abandoned, and food, clothing, and trade all depend on Chengdu—it is obvious that these people cannot be conscripted for labor.

sentences.zh: 可稅賦者，獨成都、彭、蜀、漢四州而已，以四州耗殘當十州之役，其弊可見。

translations.literal: Those from whom taxes can be collected are only the four prefectures of Chengdu, Peng, Shu, and Han. To have four exhausted prefectures bear the labor obligations of ten—the harm is evident.
translations.idiomatic: Only the four prefectures of Chengdu, Peng, Shu, and Han can still yield tax revenue. To have four depleted prefectures bear the labor obligations of ten—the harm is plain to see.

sentences.zh: 而言利者，枘鑿萬端，窮朝抵夕，千案百牘，皆取之民，官吏懼譴，責及鄰保，威以罰抶，而逋逃益滋。

translations.literal: Yet those who speak of profit devise countless schemes from morning till night. A thousand cases and a hundred documents all extract from the people. Officials fear punishment and extend responsibility to neighboring households, enforcing compliance with beatings, while flight and evasion only increase.
translations.idiomatic: Yet those who speak of profit devise endless schemes from dawn to dusk. A thousand cases and a hundred documents all extract from the people. Officials fear punishment and extend liability to neighboring households, enforcing compliance with beatings, while flight and evasion only grow worse.

sentences.zh: 又關中比饑，士人流入蜀者道路相系，地入有訖，而科斂無涯，為蜀計者，不亦難哉！

translations.literal: Moreover, Guanzhong has lately suffered famine, and scholars flowing into Shu fill the roads in an unbroken line. The land has its limits, yet levies and collections know no bounds—for those planning on behalf of Shu, is this not difficult indeed!
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Guanzhong has lately suffered famine, and refugees streaming into Shu fill the roads without end. The land has its limits, yet levies and collections know no bounds—for those planning on behalf of Shu, is this not a grave difficulty!

sentences.zh: 又平戎以西數城，皆窮山之顛，蹊隧險絕，運糧束馬之路，坐甲無人之鄉。

translations.literal: Furthermore, several cities west of Pingrong stand atop barren mountain peaks, with paths and passes perilously steep. The routes for transporting grain and leading horses are places where troops sit idle in uninhabited country.
translations.idiomatic: Furthermore, several cities west of Pingrong stand atop barren mountain peaks, with paths and passes perilously steep. The routes for transporting grain and leading horses are places where troops sit idle in uninhabited wilderness.

sentences.zh: 為戎狄言，不足利戎狄；

translations.literal: Speaking from the barbarians' perspective, they are not worth the benefit to the barbarians;
translations.idiomatic: From the barbarians' point of view, they offer no real advantage to the barbarians;

sentences.zh: 為國家言，不足廣土宇。

translations.literal: Speaking from the state's perspective, they are not worth expanding the territory.
translations.idiomatic: From the state's point of view, they are not worth expanding the realm.

sentences.zh: 柰何以彈丸地而困全蜀太平之人哉？

translations.literal: Why then use a patch of land no larger than a pellet to burden all the peaceful people of Shu?
translations.idiomatic: Why then use a patch of land no larger than a pellet to burden all the peaceful people of Shu?

sentences.zh: 若謂已戍之城不可廢，已屯之兵不可收，願罷東川，以一劍南並力從事。

translations.literal: If it is said that garrisoned cities cannot be abandoned and stationed troops cannot be withdrawn, I beg that Eastern Chuan be abolished so that all of Jiannan may combine its strength in one effort.
translations.idiomatic: If it is argued that garrisoned cities cannot be abandoned and stationed troops cannot be withdrawn, I ask that Eastern Chuan be abolished so that all of Jiannan may combine its strength in a single effort.

sentences.zh: 不爾，非陛下洗蕩關東清逆亂之意也。

translations.literal: Otherwise, this is not in accord with Your Majesty's intent to sweep clean the east of the pass and purge rebellion and disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise, this is not in keeping with Your Majesty's intent to sweep clean the region east of the pass and purge rebellion and disorder.

sentences.zh: 蜀人又擾，則貽朝廷憂。」

translations.literal: If the people of Shu are further disturbed, it will bring worry upon the court.
translations.idiomatic: If the people of Shu are further disturbed, it will only add to the court's burdens.

sentences.zh: 帝不納。

translations.literal: The emperor did not accept [the proposal].
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not accept the proposal.

sentences.zh: 梓屯將段子璋反，適從崔光遠討斬之。

translations.literal: Duan Zizhang, a garrison commander at Zi, rebelled. Gao Shi followed Cui Guangyuan in campaigning against him and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Zizhang, a garrison commander at Zi, rebelled. Gao Shi joined Cui Guangyuan in the campaign against him and had him beheaded.

sentences.zh: 而光遠兵不戢，遂大略，天子怒，罷光遠，以適代為西川節度使。

translations.literal: But Guangyuan's troops were not restrained and proceeded to plunder on a large scale. The Son of Heaven was angered, removed Guangyuan, and replaced him with Gao Shi as military commissioner of Western Chuan.
translations.idiomatic: But Guangyuan's troops were not kept in check and proceeded to plunder on a large scale. The emperor was enraged, dismissed Guangyuan, and appointed Gao Shi in his place as military commissioner of Western Chuan.

sentences.zh: 廣德元年，吐蕃取隴右，適率兵出南鄙，欲牽制其力，既無功，遂亡松、維二州及雲山城。

translations.literal: In the first year of Guangde, Tibet seized Longyou. Gao Shi led troops out from the southern frontier, intending to divert their strength, but achieved nothing and lost the two prefectures of Song and Wei and Yunshan Fort.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Guangde reign, Tibet seized Longyou. Gao Shi led troops out from the southern frontier, hoping to divert Tibetan strength, but achieved nothing and lost the prefectures of Song and Wei and Yunshan Fort.

sentences.zh: 召還，為刑部侍郎、左散騎常侍，封渤海縣侯。

translations.literal: He was recalled and appointed Vice Minister of Justice and Left Regular Attendant, and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Bohai County.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled and appointed Vice Minister of Justice and Left Regular Attendant, and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Bohai County.

sentences.zh: 永泰元年卒，贈禮部尚書，謚曰忠。

translations.literal: He died in the first year of Yongtai and was posthumously appointed Minister of Rites, with the posthumous title Loyal.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the first year of the Yongtai reign and was posthumously appointed Minister of Rites, with the posthumous title Loyal.

sentences.zh: 適尚節義，語王霸袞袞不厭。

translations.literal: Gao Shi valued integrity and righteousness and never tired of speaking of kingship and hegemony.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Shi prized integrity and righteousness and never tired of discourse on kingship and hegemony.

sentences.zh: 遭時多難，以功名自許，而言浮其術，不為搢紳所推。

translations.literal: Encountering an age of many hardships, he pledged himself to merit and fame, yet his words exceeded his abilities and he was not esteemed by the gentry.
translations.idiomatic: Living in an age of turmoil, he pledged himself to merit and fame, yet his rhetoric outran his abilities and he was not held in esteem by the gentry.

sentences.zh: 然政寬簡，所涖，人便之。

translations.literal: Yet his governance was lenient and simple, and wherever he served, the people found it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his governance was lenient and straightforward, and wherever he served, the people found life easier.

sentences.zh: 年五十始為詩，即工，以氣質自高。

translations.literal: He did not begin writing poetry until the age of fifty, yet at once proved accomplished, holding himself high through the force of his character.
translations.idiomatic: He did not begin writing poetry until the age of fifty, yet at once proved accomplished, holding himself aloft through the force of his character.

sentences.zh: 每一篇已，好事者輒傳布。

translations.literal: As soon as each poem was finished, enthusiasts would circulate it.
translations.idiomatic: As soon as each poem was finished, enthusiasts would spread it abroad.

sentences.zh: 其詒書賀蘭進明，使救梁、宋以親諸軍，與許叔冀書，令釋憾；

translations.literal: He sent a letter to Helan Jinming urging him to rescue Liang and Song and thereby win the affection of the various armies, and wrote to Xu Shuji ordering him to set aside resentment;
translations.idiomatic: He sent a letter to Helan Jinming urging him to rescue Liang and Song and thereby win the loyalty of the various armies, and wrote to Xu Shuji instructing him to set aside old grievances;

sentences.zh: 未度淮，移檄將校，絕永王，俾各自白，君子以為義而知變。

translations.literal: before crossing the Huai, he issued a proclamation to officers and commanders cutting off the Prince of Yong and ordering each to declare his own loyalty. Men of principle regarded this as righteous and discerning of changing circumstances.
translations.idiomatic: before crossing the Huai, he issued a proclamation to officers and commanders severing ties with the Prince of Yong and ordering each to declare his own loyalty. Men of principle regarded this as righteous and discerning in changing circumstances.

sentences.zh: 元結，後魏常山王遵十五代孫。

translations.literal: Yuan Jie was a fifteenth-generation descendant of Zun, Prince of Changshan of Later Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Jie was a fifteenth-generation descendant of Zun, Prince of Changshan of Northern Wei.

sentences.zh: 曾祖仁基，字惟固，從太宗征遼東，以功賜宜君田二十頃，遼口並馬牝牡各五十，拜寧塞令，襲常山公。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Renji, styled Weigu, followed Emperor Taizong in the campaign against Liaodong. For his merit he was granted twenty qing of fields at Yijun, fifty mares and fifty stallions at Liaokou, appointed magistrate of Ningsai, and inherited the title Duke of Changshan.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Renji, courtesy name Weigu, followed Emperor Taizong in the campaign against Liaodong. For his merit he was granted twenty qing of fields at Yijun, fifty mares and fifty stallions at Liaokou, appointed magistrate of Ningsai, and inherited the title Duke of Changshan.

sentences.zh: 祖亨，字利貞，美姿儀。

translations.literal: His grandfather Heng, styled Lizhen, was handsome in bearing.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Heng, courtesy name Lizhen, was handsome in bearing.

sentences.zh: 嘗曰：「我承王公餘烈，鷹犬聲樂是習，吾當以儒學易之。」

translations.literal: He once said: "I inherit the legacy of kings and dukes and am accustomed to hawking, hunting, music, and pleasure—I ought to replace these with Confucian learning.
translations.idiomatic: He once said: "I inherit the legacy of kings and dukes and am accustomed to hawking, hunting, music, and pleasure—I ought to replace all of this with Confucian learning.

sentences.zh: 霍王元軌聞其名，辟參軍事。

translations.literal: Prince Huo Yuan Gui heard of his name and recruited him as a staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Huo Yuan Gui heard of his reputation and recruited him as a staff officer.

sentences.zh: 父延祖，三歲而孤，仁基敕其母曰：「此兒且祀我。」

translations.literal: His father Yanzu was orphaned at the age of three. Renji instructed his mother: "This child will someday perform sacrifices for me.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yanzu was orphaned at the age of three. Renji told his mother: "This child will someday perform sacrifices for me.

sentences.zh: 因名而字之。

translations.literal: Accordingly he gave him his name and courtesy name.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly he gave him his name and courtesy name.

sentences.zh: 逮長，不仕，年過四十，親婭強勸之，再調舂陵丞，輒棄官去，曰：「人生衣食，可適饑飽，不宜復有所須。」

translations.literal: When he grew up, he did not take office. After passing forty, relatives by marriage strongly urged him, and he was twice assigned as assistant magistrate of Chunling, but each time he abandoned his post and left, saying: "Food and clothing in life need only satisfy hunger and fill the belly—one ought not to desire anything more.
translations.idiomatic: When he grew up, he refused to serve in office. After passing forty, relatives by marriage strongly urged him, and he was twice assigned as assistant magistrate of Chunling, but each time he resigned and left, saying: "Food and clothing in life need only satisfy hunger—one ought not to desire anything more.

sentences.zh: 每灌畦掇薪，以為「有生之役，過此吾不思也」。

translations.literal: Each time he watered his garden beds and gathered firewood, he would say: "These are the labors of life; beyond this I desire nothing."
translations.idiomatic: Each time he watered his garden beds and gathered firewood, he would say: "These are the labors of life; beyond this I desire nothing."

sentences.zh: 安祿山反，召結戒曰：「而曹逢世多故，不得自安山林，勉樹名節，無近羞辱」雲。

translations.literal: When An Lushan rebelled, he summoned Jie and admonished him: "You encounter an age of many troubles and cannot rest secure in mountain forests. Strive to establish a reputation for integrity and do not draw near to disgrace," and so on.
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan rebelled, he summoned Jie and admonished him: "You live in an age of turmoil and cannot rest secure in the mountains. Strive to establish a reputation for integrity and do not bring disgrace upon yourself," and so forth.

sentences.zh: 卒年七十六，門人私謚曰太先生。

translations.literal: He died at the age of seventy-six. His disciples privately gave him the posthumous title Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of seventy-six. His disciples privately gave him the posthumous title Grand Master.

sentences.zh: 結少不羈，十七乃折節向學，事元德秀。

translations.literal: Jie was unrestrained in youth; only at seventeen did he restrain himself and turn to study, serving Yuan Dexiu as his teacher.
translations.idiomatic: Jie was wild in youth; only at seventeen did he restrain himself and turn to study, taking Yuan Dexiu as his teacher.

sentences.zh: 天寶十二載舉進士，禮部侍郎陽浚見其文，曰：「一第慁子耳，有司得子是賴！」

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Tianbao he passed the jinshi examination. Yang Jun, Vice Minister of Rites, saw his essays and said: "A degree would merely sully the man—the examiners would be fortunate to have him!
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of the Tianbao reign he passed the jinshi examination. Yang Jun, Vice Minister of Rites, saw his essays and said: "A degree would merely sully the man—the examiners would be fortunate to have him!

sentences.zh: 果擢上第。

translations.literal: He was indeed placed at the top of the list.
translations.idiomatic: He was indeed placed at the top of the list.

sentences.zh: 復舉制科。

translations.literal: He also passed the special decree examination.
translations.idiomatic: He also passed the special decree examination.

sentences.zh: 會天下亂，沈浮人間。

translations.literal: Just then the empire fell into disorder, and he drifted through the world.
translations.idiomatic: Just then the empire fell into disorder, and he drifted through the world.

sentences.zh: 國子司業蘇源明見肅宗，問天下士，薦結可用。

translations.literal: Su Yuanming, Vice Director of the Directorate of Education, had an audience with Emperor Suzong, who asked about men of talent throughout the realm. Yuanming recommended Jie as capable.
translations.idiomatic: Su Yuanming, Vice Director of the Directorate of Education, had an audience with Emperor Suzong, who asked about men of talent throughout the realm. Yuanming recommended Jie as capable.

sentences.zh: 時史思明攻河陽，帝將幸河東，召結詣京師，問所欲言，結自以始見軒陛，拘忌諱，恐言不悉情，乃上《時議》三篇。

translations.literal: At that time Shi Siming was attacking Heyang, and the emperor was about to visit Hedong. Jie was summoned to the capital and asked what he wished to say. Jie felt that, having just been received at the imperial throne for the first time, he was constrained by taboos and feared his words would not fully express his meaning, and so submitted three essays entitled "Contemporary Discourse."
translations.idiomatic: At that time Shi Siming was attacking Heyang, and the emperor was about to visit Hedong. Jie was summoned to the capital and asked what he wished to say. sentences.zh: 議者問：「往年逆賊，東窮海，南淮、漢，西抵函、秦，北徹幽都，醜徒狼扈，在四方者幾百萬，當時之禍可謂劇，而人心危矣。

translations.literal: The questioner asked: "In former years the rebel bandits ranged east to the sea, south to the Huai and Han, west to Hangu and Qin, and north to Youdu. The vile mob ran wild, and those in the four directions numbered nearly a million. The calamity of that time could be called severe, and the hearts of men were in peril.
translations.idiomatic: The questioner asked: "In former years the rebel bandits ranged east to the sea, south to the Huai and Han, west to Hangu and Qin, and north to Youdu. The vile mob ran wild, and those in the four directions numbered nearly a million. The calamity of that time was severe indeed, and the hearts of men were in peril.

sentences.zh: 天子獨以匹馬至靈武，合弱旅，鉏強寇，師及渭西，曾不逾時，摧銳攘兇，復兩京，收河南州縣，何其易邪？

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven alone rode a single horse to Lingwu, gathered a weak force, uprooted a strong enemy, and when his army reached west of the Wei, in no more than the usual span of time crushed the sharp and expelled the vicious, recovered the two capitals, and retook the prefectures and counties of Henan—how easy was that!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor alone rode a single horse to Lingwu, gathered a weak force, uprooted a powerful enemy, and when his army reached west of the Wei, in scarcely any time at all crushed the enemy and recovered the two capitals and the prefectures and counties of Henan—how easily was that accomplished!

sentences.zh: 乃今河北奸逆不盡，山林江湖亡命尚多，盜賊數犯州縣，百姓轉徙，踵系不絕，將士臨敵而奔，賢人君子遁逃不出。

translations.literal: Yet now the traitors of Hebei are not yet eliminated, fugitives in mountains, forests, rivers, and lakes are still numerous, bandits repeatedly attack prefectures and counties, the people move about in unending flight, soldiers flee when facing the enemy, and worthy men and gentlemen hide and do not emerge.
translations.idiomatic: Yet now the traitors of Hebei are not yet eliminated, fugitives in mountains, forests, rivers, and lakes are still numerous, bandits repeatedly attack prefectures and counties, refugees move in an unending stream, soldiers flee when facing the enemy, and worthy men and gentlemen hide and do not emerge.

sentences.zh: 陛下往在靈武、鳳翔，無今日勝兵而能殺敵，無今日檢禁而無亡命，無今日威令而盜賊不作，無今日財用而百姓不流，無今日爵賞而士不散，無今日朝廷而賢者思仕，何哉？

translations.literal: When Your Majesty was formerly at Lingwu and Fengxiang, you had none of today's victorious troops yet could kill the enemy; none of today's strict prohibitions yet had no fugitives; none of today's awe-inspiring commands yet bandits did not arise; none of today's wealth yet the people did not flee; none of today's ranks and rewards yet scholars did not scatter; none of today's court yet worthy men wished to serve—why?
translations.idiomatic: When Your Majesty was at Lingwu and Fengxiang, you had none of today's victorious troops yet could defeat the enemy; none of today's strict prohibitions yet had no fugitives; none of today's authority yet bandits did not arise; none of today's wealth yet the people did not flee; none of today's ranks and rewards yet scholars did not scatter; none of today's court yet worthy men wished to serve—why?

sentences.zh: 將天子能以危為安，而忍以未安忘危邪？」

translations.literal: Could it be that the Son of Heaven was able to turn peril into safety then, yet now tolerates forgetting peril while still not at safety?
translations.idiomatic: Could it be that the emperor was able to turn peril into safety then, yet now tolerates forgetting danger while still not secure?

sentences.zh: 對曰：「此非難言之。

translations.literal: The reply was: "This is not difficult to explain.
translations.idiomatic: The reply was: "This is not difficult to explain.

sentences.zh: 前日天子恨愧陵廟為羯逆傷汙，憤悵上皇南幸巴、蜀，隱悼宗戚見誅，側身勤勞，不憚親撫士卒，與人權位，信而不疑，渴聞忠直，過弗諱改。

translations.literal: In former days the Son of Heaven hated and grieved that the imperial tombs and temples had been defiled by the Jie rebels, was indignant and distressed that the Retired Emperor had fled south to Ba and Shu, mourned in secret that imperial clansmen had been executed, bent himself to labor, did not shrink from personally comforting the troops, shared power and rank with others, trusted without doubt, thirsted to hear loyal and straight words, and did not conceal faults but corrected them.
translations.idiomatic: In former days the emperor hated and grieved that the imperial tombs and temples had been defiled by the Jie rebels, was indignant that the Retired Emperor had fled south to Ba and Shu, mourned in secret that imperial clansmen had been executed, bent himself to labor, did not shrink from personally comforting the troops, shared power and rank with others, trusted without doubt, thirsted to hear loyal and straight counsel, and did not conceal faults but corrected them.

sentences.zh: 此以弱制強，以危取安之繇也。

translations.literal: This was the means by which the weak overcame the strong and peril was turned into safety.
translations.idiomatic: This was how the weak overcame the strong and peril was turned into safety.

sentences.zh: 今天子重城深宮，燕和而居；

translations.literal: Today the Son of Heaven dwells in layered walls and deep palaces, living in ease and harmony;
translations.idiomatic: Today the emperor dwells in layered walls and deep palaces, living in ease and harmony;

sentences.zh: 凝冕大昕，纓佩而朝；

translations.literal: donning the crown at the great dawn audience, cap-strings and jade pendants in attendance at court;
translations.idiomatic: donning the crown at the great dawn audience, cap-strings and jade pendants in attendance at court;

sentences.zh: 太官具味，視時而獻，太常備樂，和聲以薦；

translations.literal: the Grand Provisioner prepares delicacies and presents them according to the season, the Grand Master of Ceremonies prepares music and offers harmonious sounds;
translations.idiomatic: the Grand Provisioner prepares delicacies and presents them according to the season, the Grand Master of Ceremonies prepares music and offers harmonious sounds;

sentences.zh: 國機軍務，參籌乃敢進；

translations.literal: state affairs and military matters are presented only after consultation;
translations.idiomatic: state affairs and military matters are presented only after consultation;

sentences.zh: 百姓疾苦，時有不聞；

translations.literal: the sufferings of the people are sometimes not heard;
translations.idiomatic: the sufferings of the people are sometimes not heard;

sentences.zh: 廄芻良馬、宮籍美女、輿服禮物、休符瑞諜，日月充備；

translations.literal: stable fodder and fine horses, palace registers of beautiful women, carriages, robes, gifts, auspicious omens and propitious signs—all are fully supplied day by day;
translations.idiomatic: stable fodder and fine horses, palace registers of beautiful women, carriages, robes, gifts, auspicious omens and propitious signs—all are fully supplied day by day;

sentences.zh: 朝廷歌頌盛德大業，聽而不厭；

translations.literal: the court sings hymns of great virtue and grand achievement, listening without weariness;
translations.idiomatic: the court sings hymns of great virtue and grand achievement, listening without weariness;

sentences.zh: 四方貢賦，爭上尤異；

translations.literal: tribute and taxes from the four directions vie to offer the most extraordinary items;
translations.idiomatic: tribute and taxes from the four directions vie to offer the most extraordinary items;

sentences.zh: 諧臣顐官，怡愉天顏；

translations.literal: ingratiating ministers and obsequious officials delight the imperial countenance;
translations.idiomatic: ingratiating ministers and obsequious officials delight the imperial countenance;

sentences.zh: 文武大臣至於庶官，皆權賞逾望。

translations.literal: from civil and military grandees down to common officials, all receive power and rewards beyond their expectations.
translations.idiomatic: from civil and military grandees down to common officials, all receive power and rewards beyond their expectations.

sentences.zh: 此所以不能以強制弱，以未安忘危。

translations.literal: This is why the strong cannot overcome the weak and why peril is forgotten while safety is not yet achieved.
translations.idiomatic: This is why the strong cannot overcome the weak and why danger is forgotten while security is not yet achieved.

sentences.zh: 若陛下視今日之安，能如靈武時，何寇盜強弱可言哉！」

translations.literal: If Your Majesty could regard today's peace as you did at Lingwu, what talk would there be of bandits, robbers, strong, or weak!"
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty could regard today's peace as you did at Lingwu, what talk would there be of bandits, robbers, strong, or weak!"

translations.literal: The questioner said: "I have heard that scholars consult among themselves: 'Formerly, when we followed the Son of Heaven in resisting the vicious rebels, victory meant both family and state preserved, defeat meant both destroyed. Therefore life and death were decided in battle, and right and wrong were pushed to the limit in remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: The questioner said: "I have heard that scholars consult among themselves: 'Formerly, when we followed the emperor in resisting the vicious rebels, victory meant both family and state preserved, defeat meant both destroyed. sentences.zh: 今吾名位重，財貨足，爵賞厚，勤勞已極，外無仇讎害我，內無窮賤迫我，何苦當鋒刃以近死，忤人主以近禍乎？』

translations.literal: Now our names and ranks are high, our wealth sufficient, our titles and rewards generous, our labors already at their utmost. Outside there are no enemies to harm us; inside there are no poor and lowly pressing upon us. Why should we suffer the blade's edge and approach death, or offend the sovereign and approach disaster?
translations.idiomatic: Now our names and ranks are high, our wealth sufficient, our titles and rewards generous, our labors already at their utmost. sentences.zh: 又聞曰：『吾州裏有病父老母、孤兄寡婦，皆力役乞丐，凍餒不足，況於死者，人誰哀之？』

translations.literal: I have also heard: 'In our district and village there are sick fathers and old mothers, orphaned brothers and widowed sisters, all conscripted for labor and reduced to begging, with cold and hunger unrelieved. As for the dead, who would mourn them?'
translations.idiomatic: I have also heard: 'In our district and village there are sick fathers and old mothers, orphaned brothers and widowed sisters, all conscripted for labor and reduced to begging, with cold and hunger unrelieved. As for the dead, who would mourn them?'

translations.literal: I have also heard: 'The realm is shattered, the common people are in peril and distress. Those who bear taxes and labor service are all the weak, poor, and alone, fleeing, dying, and migrating, grief and sorrow filling the roads—this too has reached its limit.'
translations.idiomatic: I have also heard: 'The realm is shattered, the common people are in peril and distress. Those who bear taxes and labor service are all the weak, poor, and alone, fleeing, dying, and migrating, grief and sorrow filling the roads—this too has reached its limit.'

sentences.zh: 天下安，我等豈無畎畝自處？

translations.literal: If the realm were at peace, would we not each have fields to live on?
translations.idiomatic: If the realm were at peace, would we not each have fields to live on?

sentences.zh: 若不安，我不復以忠義仁信方直死矣！』

translations.literal: If it is not at peace, we will no longer die for loyalty, righteousness, benevolence, trustworthiness, uprightness, and integrity!
translations.idiomatic: If it is not at peace, we will no longer die for loyalty, righteousness, benevolence, trustworthiness, uprightness, and integrity!

sentences.zh: 人且如此，奈何？」

translations.literal: People are already like this—what is to be done?
translations.idiomatic: People are already like this—what is to be done?

sentences.zh: 對曰：「國家非欲其然，蓋失於太明太信耳。

translations.literal: The reply was: "The state does not desire this to be so; it has simply failed through being too perspicacious and too trusting.
translations.idiomatic: The reply was: "The state does not desire this to be so; it has simply failed through being too perspicacious and too trusting.

sentences.zh: 夫太明則見其內情，將藏內情則罔惑生下。

translations.literal: When one is too perspicacious, inner feelings are exposed; wishing to conceal inner feelings, deception and confusion arise below.
translations.idiomatic: When one is too perspicacious, inner feelings are exposed; wishing to conceal inner feelings, deception and confusion arise below.

sentences.zh: 能令必信，信可必矣，而太信之中，至奸尤惡之。

translations.literal: When orders must be believed, belief can be assured—but within excessive trust, the most treacherous especially detest it.
translations.idiomatic: When orders must be believed, belief can be assured—but within excessive trust, the most treacherous especially detest it.

sentences.zh: 如此遂使朝廷亡公直，天下失忠信，蒼生益冤結。

translations.literal: In this way the court loses public uprightness, the realm loses loyalty and trust, and the common people grow ever more aggrieved and resentful.
translations.idiomatic: In this way the court loses public uprightness, the realm loses loyalty and trust, and the common people grow ever more aggrieved and resentful.

sentences.zh: 將欲治之，能無端由？

translations.literal: If one wishes to govern this, can there be no root cause?
translations.idiomatic: If one wishes to remedy this, can there be no root cause?

sentences.zh: 吾等議於野，又何所及？」

translations.literal: We discuss in the open fields—what can we reach?"
translations.idiomatic: We discuss in the open fields—what can we accomplish?"

translations.literal: The questioner said: "Your Majesty thinks of settling the common people, destroying traitors and rebels, and seeking great peace, laboring in mind and exhausting your spirit—for four years now. Yet those who speak of it find it strange. Why?
translations.idiomatic: The questioner said: "Your Majesty thinks of settling the common people, destroying traitors and rebels, and seeking great peace, laboring in mind and exhausting your spirit—for four years now. Yet those who speak of it find it strange. Why?

sentences.zh: 對曰：「如天子所思，說者所異，非不知之。

translations.literal: The reply was: "As for what the Son of Heaven thinks and what the speakers find strange, [the people] are not unaware of it.
translations.idiomatic: The reply was: "As for what the emperor thinks and what the speakers find strange, the people are not unaware of it.

sentences.zh: 凡有詔令丁寧事皆不行，空言一再，頗類諧戲。

translations.literal: Whenever there are edicts with repeated earnest admonitions, none are carried out. Empty words are repeated again and again, much like jesting.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever there are edicts with repeated earnest admonitions, none are carried out. Empty words are repeated again and again, much like jesting.

sentences.zh: 今有仁恤之令，憂勤之誥，人皆族立黨語，指而議之。

translations.literal: Now there are orders of benevolent relief and proclamations of anxious diligence, yet people all gather in clans and speak in factions, pointing and discussing them.
translations.idiomatic: Now there are orders of benevolent relief and proclamations of anxious diligence, yet people all gather in groups and speak in factions, pointing and discussing them.

sentences.zh: 天子不知其然，以為言雖不行，猶足以勸。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven does not know this to be so, thinking that though words are not carried out, they still suffice to encourage.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor does not know this to be so, thinking that though words are not carried out, they still suffice to encourage.

sentences.zh: 彼沮勸，在乎明審均當而必行也。

translations.literal: Whether they are discouraged or encouraged depends on clarity, fairness, appropriateness, and certain execution.
translations.idiomatic: Whether they are discouraged or encouraged depends on clarity, fairness, appropriateness, and certain execution.

sentences.zh: 天子能行已言之令，必將來之法，雜徭弊制，拘忌煩令，一切蠲蕩，任天下賢士，屏斥小人，然後推仁信威令，謹行不惑。

translations.literal: If the Son of Heaven can carry out the orders already spoken and the laws yet to come, sweep away all mixed corvée, corrupt institutions, restrictive taboos, and vexatious commands, employ worthy men throughout the realm and banish petty men, and then extend benevolence, trust, authority, and commands, executing them carefully without confusion—

translations.idiomatic: this is the constant way of emperors and kings—why should it not be attained?"

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased and said: "You can dispel my worries.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased and said: "You can dispel my worries.

sentences.zh: 擢右金吾兵曹參軍，攝監察御史，為山南西道節度參謀。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Right Jinwu Corps Army Staff Assistant, acting Censor, and staff officer to the military commissioner of Shannan West Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Right Jinwu Corps Army Staff Assistant, acting Censor, and staff officer to the military commissioner of Shannan West Circuit.

sentences.zh: 募義士於唐、鄧、汝、蔡，降劇賊五千，瘞戰死露胔於泌南，名曰哀丘。

translations.literal: He recruited volunteers in Tang, Deng, Ru, and Cai, accepting the surrender of five thousand fierce rebels. He buried the exposed corpses of the war dead south of Bi and named the mound Mound of Lament.
translations.idiomatic: He recruited volunteers in Tang, Deng, Ru, and Cai, accepting the surrender of five thousand fierce rebels. He buried the exposed corpses of the war dead south of Bi and named the mound Mound of Lament.

sentences.zh: 史思明亂，帝將親征，結建言：「賊銳不可與爭，宜折以謀。」

translations.literal: When Shi Siming rebelled, the emperor was about to campaign in person. Jie submitted advice: "The rebels are sharp and cannot be contested directly; they should be broken by strategy.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Siming rebelled, the emperor was about to campaign in person. Jie submitted advice: "The rebels are sharp and cannot be contested directly; they should be broken by strategy.

sentences.zh: 帝善之，因命發宛、葉軍挫賊南鋒，結屯泌陽守險，全十五城。

translations.literal: The emperor approved this and ordered troops from Wan and Ye to blunt the rebels' southern vanguard. Jie encamped at Biyang to hold the passes and preserved fifteen cities.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved this and ordered troops from Wan and Ye to blunt the rebels' southern vanguard. Jie encamped at Biyang to hold the passes and preserved fifteen cities.

sentences.zh: 以討賊功遷監察御史裏行。

translations.literal: For his merit in suppressing the rebels he was transferred to Censor, Acting.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit in suppressing the rebels he was transferred to Censor, Acting.

translations.idiomatic: Lü Yun, military commissioner of Jingnan, requested additional troops to resist the rebels. The emperor promoted Jie to Vice Director of the Water Bureau and assigned him to Yun's staff.

translations.idiomatic: He also served on the staff of Lai Tian of Shannan East Circuit. At that time there were parents accompanying their sons in the army. Jie said to Tian: "Those who are filial and benevolent may be spoken to of loyalty;

translations.idiomatic: Would they be blamed for loyalty, trustworthiness, righteousness, and courage yet not encouraged in filial piety and kindness?

translations.idiomatic: When Tian was executed, Jie took charge of the headquarters affairs.

translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Daizong ascended the throne, Jie firmly declined and begged to return to Fanshang to attend his parents.

translations.literal: Cishan is Jie's courtesy name.
translations.idiomatic: Cishan is Jie's courtesy name.

sentences.zh: 世業載國史，世系在家諜。

translations.literal: The family's achievements are recorded in the national histories; the family lineage is in the household register.
translations.idiomatic: The family's achievements are recorded in the national histories; the family lineage is in the household register.

sentences.zh: 少居商餘山，著《元子》十篇，故以元子為稱。

translations.literal: In youth he lived on Shangyu Mountain and wrote ten chapters of "The Yuan Son," and so took Yuan Son as his appellation.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he lived on Shangyu Mountain and wrote ten chapters of "The Yuan Son," and so took Yuan Son as his appellation.

sentences.zh: 天下兵興，逃亂入猗於洞，始稱猗於子。

translations.literal: When warfare arose throughout the realm, he fled the turmoil and entered Yiyu Cave, and first styled himself the Yiyu Son.
translations.idiomatic: When warfare arose throughout the realm, he fled the turmoil and entered Yiyu Cave, and first styled himself the Yiyu Son.

sentences.zh: 後家濱，乃自稱浪士。

translations.literal: Later he made his home on the riverbank and styled himself the Wave Scholar.
translations.idiomatic: Later he made his home on the riverbank and styled himself the Wave Scholar.

sentences.zh: 及有官，人以為浪者亦漫為官乎，呼為漫郎。

translations.literal: When he received office, people thought that one who was wave-like would also drift through office, and called him the Drifting Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: When he received office, people thought that one who was wave-like would also drift through office, and called him the Drifting Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 既客樊上，漫遂顯。

translations.literal: After he became a guest at Fanshang, the drifting became manifest.
translations.idiomatic: After he became a guest at Fanshang, the drifting became manifest.

sentences.zh: 樊左右皆漁者，少長相戲，更曰聱叟。

translations.literal: Those around Fan were all fishermen. Young and old joked with one another and in turn called him the Stubborn Old Man.
translations.idiomatic: Those around Fan were all fishermen. Young and old joked with one another and in turn called him the Stubborn Old Man.

sentences.zh: 彼誚以聱者，為其不相從聽，不相鉤加，帶笭箵而盡船，獨聱齖而揮車。

translations.literal: They mocked him as stubborn because he would not follow along and listen, would not join in hooking and hauling, wore a fish basket while others filled their boats, and alone was stubborn and tooth-gnashing while driving his cart.
translations.idiomatic: They mocked him as stubborn because he would not follow along and listen, would not join in hooking and hauling, wore a fish basket while others filled their boats, and alone was stubborn and tooth-gnashing while driving his cart.

sentences.zh: 酒徒得此，又曰：「公之漫其猶聱乎？

translations.literal: The drinking companions got hold of this and said again: "Is the gentleman's drifting not like being stubborn?
translations.idiomatic: The drinking companions got hold of this and said again: "Is the gentleman's drifting not like being stubborn?

sentences.zh: 公守著作，不帶笭箵乎？

translations.literal: The gentleman holds the post of Compiler—does he not wear a fish basket?
translations.idiomatic: The gentleman holds the post of Compiler—does he not wear a fish basket?

sentences.zh: 又漫浪於人間，得非聱齖乎？

translations.literal: And drifting freely among men—is that not being stubborn and tooth-gnashing?
translations.idiomatic: And drifting freely among men—is that not being stubborn and tooth-gnashing?

sentences.zh: 公漫久矣，可以漫為叟。」

translations.literal: The gentleman has drifted long—he may be called the Drifting Old Man.
translations.idiomatic: The gentleman has drifted long—he may be called the Drifting Old Man.

sentences.zh: 於戲！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 吾不從聽於時俗，不鉤加於當世，誰是聱者，吾欲從之！

translations.literal: I do not follow along and listen to the fashions of the age, nor join in hooking and hauling with the present world. Who is the stubborn one? I wish to follow him!
translations.idiomatic: I do not follow along and listen to the fashions of the age, nor join in hooking and hauling with the present world. Who is the stubborn one? I wish to follow him!

sentences.zh: 彼聱叟不慚帶乎笭箵，吾又安能薄乎著作？

translations.literal: That stubborn old man is not ashamed to wear a fish basket—how can I look down on the post of Compiler?
translations.idiomatic: That stubborn old man is not ashamed to wear a fish basket—how can I look down on the post of Compiler?

sentences.zh: 彼聱叟不羞聱齖於鄰裏，吾又安能慚漫浪於人間？

translations.literal: That stubborn old man is not ashamed to be stubborn and tooth-gnashing among his neighbors—how can I be ashamed to drift freely among men?
translations.idiomatic: That stubborn old man is not ashamed to be stubborn and tooth-gnashing among his neighbors—how can I be ashamed to drift freely among men?

sentences.zh: 取而醉人議，當以漫叟為稱。

translations.literal: Taking the drunkards' discussion, I should take the Drifting Old Man as my appellation.
translations.idiomatic: Taking the drunkards' discussion, I should take the Drifting Old Man as my appellation.

sentences.zh: 直荒浪其情性，誕漫其所為，使人知無所存有，無所將待。

translations.literal: Let my disposition be wild and drifting, my actions broad and unrestrained, so that people know I possess nothing and await nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Let my disposition be wild and drifting, my actions broad and unrestrained, so that people know I possess nothing and await nothing.

sentences.zh: 乃為語曰：「能帶笭箵，全獨而保生；

translations.literal: Then he composed a saying: "One who can wear a fish basket preserves himself alone and keeps his life;
translations.idiomatic: Then he composed a saying: "One who can wear a fish basket preserves himself alone and keeps his life;

sentences.zh: 能學聱齖，保宗而全家。

translations.literal: one who can learn to be stubborn and tooth-gnashing preserves his clan and keeps his family whole.
translations.idiomatic: one who can learn to be stubborn and tooth-gnashing preserves his clan and keeps his family whole.

sentences.zh: 聱也如此，漫乎非邪！」

translations.literal: To be stubborn is like this—is drifting not the same!"
translations.idiomatic: To be stubborn is like this—is drifting not the same!"

sentences.zh: 久之，拜道州刺史。

translations.literal: After some time he was appointed prefect of Dao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was appointed prefect of Dao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 初，西原蠻掠居人數萬去，遺戶裁四千，諸使調發符牒二百函，結以人困甚，不忍加賦，即上言：「臣州為賊焚破，糧儲、屋宅、男女、牛馬幾盡。

translations.literal: At first, the Xiyuan barbarians carried off tens of thousands of inhabitants. Only four thousand households remained. The various commissioners sent two hundred bundles of requisition orders. Jie, seeing the people in extreme distress, could not bear to impose further levies and submitted a memorial: "My prefecture has been burned and destroyed by bandits. Grain stores, houses, men and women, cattle and horses are nearly all gone.
translations.idiomatic: At first, the Xiyuan barbarians carried off tens of thousands of inhabitants. Only four thousand households remained. The various commissioners sent two hundred bundles of requisition orders. Jie, seeing the people in extreme distress, could not bear to impose further levies and submitted a memorial: "My prefecture has been burned and destroyed by bandits. Grain stores, houses, men and women, cattle and horses are nearly all gone.

sentences.zh: 今百姓十不一在，耄孺騷離，未有所安。

translations.literal: Now not one in ten of the common people remains. The old and the young are scattered in turmoil and have no place of peace.
translations.idiomatic: Now not one in ten of the common people remains. The old and the young are scattered in turmoil and have no place of peace.

sentences.zh: 嶺南諸州，寇盜不盡，得守捉候望四十餘屯，一有不靖，湖南且亂。

translations.literal: In the prefectures of Lingnan, bandits and robbers are not yet eliminated. There are more than forty garrison and watch posts. If one place is unsettled, Hunan will soon be in disorder.
translations.idiomatic: In the prefectures of Lingnan, bandits and robbers are not yet eliminated. There are more than forty garrison and watch posts. If one place is unsettled, Hunan will soon be in disorder.

sentences.zh: 請免百姓所負租稅及租庸使和市雜物十三萬緡。」

translations.literal: I request exemption of the taxes owed by the people and the 130,000 strings of cash for market purchases and miscellaneous goods demanded by the corvée commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: I request exemption of the taxes owed by the people and the 130,000 strings of cash for market purchases and miscellaneous goods demanded by the corvée commissioner.

sentences.zh: 帝許之。

translations.literal: The emperor granted this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor granted this.

sentences.zh: 明年，租庸使索上供十萬緡，結又奏：「歲正租庸外，所率宜以時增減。」

translations.literal: The next year the corvée commissioner demanded 100,000 strings of cash for tribute to the court. Jie submitted again: "Beyond the regular annual corvée, what is levied should be increased or decreased according to the times.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the corvée commissioner demanded 100,000 strings of cash for tribute to the court. Jie submitted again: "Beyond the regular annual corvée, what is levied should be increased or decreased according to the times.

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: An edict approved this.
translations.idiomatic: An edict approved this.

sentences.zh: 結為民營舍給田，免徭役，流亡歸者萬餘。

translations.literal: Jie built dwellings for the people and granted them fields, exempting them from corvée. More than ten thousand refugees returned.
translations.idiomatic: Jie built dwellings for the people and granted them fields, exempting them from corvée. More than ten thousand refugees returned.

sentences.zh: 進授容管經略使，身諭蠻豪，綏定八州。

translations.literal: He was promoted and appointed Military Commissioner of Rongguan, personally instructing the barbarian chieftains and pacifying eight prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted and appointed Military Commissioner of Rongguan, personally instructing the barbarian chieftains and pacifying eight prefectures.

sentences.zh: 會母喪，人皆詣節度府請留，加左金吾衛將軍。

translations.literal: When his mother died, the people all went to the military commissioner's headquarters to request that he be kept. He was additionally appointed General of the Left Jinwu Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died, the people all went to the military commissioner's headquarters to request that he be kept. He was additionally appointed General of the Left Jinwu Guard.

sentences.zh: 民樂其教，至立石頌德。

translations.literal: The people rejoiced in his governance, even erecting stone steles to praise his virtue.
translations.idiomatic: The people rejoiced in his governance, even erecting stone steles to praise his virtue.

sentences.zh: 罷還京師，卒，年五十，贈禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: After leaving office he returned to the capital and died at the age of fifty. He was posthumously appointed Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: After leaving office he returned to the capital and died at the age of fifty. He was posthumously appointed Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 李承，趙州高邑人。

translations.literal: Li Cheng was a native of Gaoyi in Zhao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Li Cheng was a native of Gaoyi in Zhao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 幼孤，其兄曄養之。

translations.literal: Orphaned in youth, he was raised by his elder brother Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned in youth, he was raised by his elder brother Ye.

sentences.zh: 既長，以悌聞。

translations.literal: When he grew up, he was known for fraternal devotion.
translations.idiomatic: When he grew up, he was known for fraternal devotion.

sentences.zh: 擢明經，遷累大理評事，為河南采訪使判官。

translations.literal: He passed the mingjing examination and was transferred through successive posts to Case Reviewer of the Court of Judicial Review, serving as aide to the Henan Investigation Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the mingjing examination and rose through successive posts to Case Reviewer of the Court of Judicial Review, serving as aide to the Henan Investigation Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 尹子奇陷汴州，拘承送洛陽，覘得賊謀，皆密啟諸朝。

translations.literal: When Yin Ziqi captured Bian Prefecture, he detained Cheng and sent him to Luoyang. Cheng observed the rebels' plans and secretly reported them all to the court.
translations.idiomatic: When Yin Ziqi captured Bian Prefecture, he detained Cheng and sent him to Luoyang. Cheng observed the rebels' plans and secretly reported them all to the court.

sentences.zh: 兩京平，例貶臨川尉。

translations.literal: When the two capitals were recovered, by precedent he was demoted to assistant magistrate of Linchuan.
translations.idiomatic: When the two capitals were recovered, by precedent he was demoted to assistant magistrate of Linchuan.

sentences.zh: 不三月，除德清令。

translations.literal: Within three months he was appointed magistrate of Deqing.
translations.idiomatic: Within three months he was appointed magistrate of Deqing.

sentences.zh: 尋擢監察御史，累遷吏部郎中，淮南西道黜陟使。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to Censor and transferred through successive posts to Director of the Personnel Bureau and Promotion-and-Demotion Commissioner of Huainan West Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was promoted to Censor and rose through successive posts to Director of the Personnel Bureau and Promotion-and-Demotion Commissioner of Huainan West Circuit.

sentences.zh: 奏置常豐堰於楚州，以禦海潮，溉屯田塉鹵，收常十倍它歲。

translations.literal: He memorialized to establish the Changfeng Dam at Chu Prefecture to repel sea tides and irrigate saline garrison fields, yielding harvests regularly ten times those of other years.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized to establish the Changfeng Dam at Chu Prefecture to repel sea tides and irrigate saline garrison fields, yielding harvests regularly ten times those of other years.

sentences.zh: 德宗將討梁崇義，李希烈揣知之，乃表崇義過惡，請先誅討，帝悅，數對左右稱其忠。

translations.literal: When Emperor Dezong was about to campaign against Liang Chongyi, Li Xilie guessed this and memorialized listing Chongyi's faults and crimes, requesting that he be punished first. The emperor was pleased and repeatedly told those around him that Xilie was loyal.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Dezong was about to campaign against Liang Chongyi, Li Xilie guessed this and memorialized listing Chongyi's faults and crimes, requesting that he be punished first. The emperor was pleased and repeatedly told those around him that Xilie was loyal.

sentences.zh: 會承使回，言希烈能立功，然恐後不可制，帝初謂不然，及崇義平，希烈果叛，始思其言，擢拜河中尹、晉絳觀察使。

translations.literal: When Cheng returned from his mission, he said that Xilie could achieve merit but feared he would later be uncontrollable. The emperor at first said this was not so. When Chongyi was pacified, Xilie indeed rebelled, and the emperor then recalled Cheng's words and promoted him to Governor of Hezhong and Observation Commissioner of Jin and Jiang.
translations.idiomatic: When Cheng returned from his mission, he said that Xilie could achieve merit but feared he would later be uncontrollable. The emperor at first said this was not so. When Chongyi was pacified, Xilie indeed rebelled, and the emperor then recalled Cheng's words and promoted him to Governor of Hezhong and Observation Commissioner of Jin and Jiang.

sentences.zh: 承廉正有雅望，以才顯於時。

translations.literal: Cheng was upright and incorruptible with an elegant reputation, distinguished for his talent in his time.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng was upright and incorruptible with an elegant reputation, distinguished for his talent in his time.

sentences.zh: 未幾，改山南東道節度使。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to military commissioner of Shannan East Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was transferred to military commissioner of Shannan East Circuit.

sentences.zh: 時希烈猶據襄州，帝慮不受命，欲以禁兵衛送承，承辭，請以單騎入。

translations.literal: At that time Xilie still held Xiang Prefecture. The emperor feared he would not accept the appointment and wished to escort Cheng with imperial troops. Cheng declined and requested to enter alone on a single horse.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Xilie still held Xiang Prefecture. The emperor feared he would not accept the appointment and wished to escort Cheng with imperial troops. Cheng declined and requested to enter alone on a single horse.

sentences.zh: 既至，希烈舍承外館，迫脅日萬端，承晏然誓以死守。

translations.literal: When he arrived, Xilie lodged Cheng in an outer guesthouse and pressed and threatened him daily in countless ways. Cheng remained calm and swore to defend to the death.
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived, Xilie lodged Cheng in an outer guesthouse and pressed and threatened him daily in countless ways. Cheng remained calm and swore to defend to the death.

sentences.zh: 希烈不能屈，遂大掠去，襄、漢蕩然。

translations.literal: Xilie could not break him and departed after plundering on a large scale. Xiang and Han were left desolate.
translations.idiomatic: Xilie could not break him and departed after plundering on a large scale. Xiang and Han were left desolate.

sentences.zh: 承輯綏撫安之，居一年，闔境完復。

translations.literal: Cheng gathered, pacified, and settled the people. Within a year the entire circuit was restored to wholeness.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng gathered, pacified, and settled the people. Within a year the entire circuit was restored to wholeness.

sentences.zh: 初，希烈雖去，留部校守覘，往來踵舍，承因得使所厚臧叔雅結希烈腹心周曾、王玢、姚詹。

translations.literal: At first, though Xilie had departed, he left subordinate officers to keep watch. They came and went in an unbroken stream at the guesthouses. Cheng thereby was able to send his close associate Zang Shuya to win over Xilie's trusted followers Zhou Zeng, Wang Bin, and Yao Zhan.
translations.idiomatic: At first, though Xilie had departed, he left subordinate officers to keep watch. They came and went in an unbroken stream at the guesthouses. Cheng thereby was able to send his close associate Zang Shuya to win over Xilie's trusted followers Zhou Zeng, Wang Bin, and Yao Zhan.

sentences.zh: 及曾等謀殺希烈，承首謀也。

translations.literal: When Zhou and the others plotted to kill Xilie, Cheng was the chief plotter.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou and the others plotted to kill Xilie, Cheng was the chief plotter.

sentences.zh: 密詔褒美。

translations.literal: A secret edict praised and commended him.
translations.idiomatic: A secret edict praised and commended him.

sentences.zh: 尋檢校工部尚書、湖南觀察使。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Acting Minister of Works and Observation Commissioner of Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed Acting Minister of Works and Observation Commissioner of Hunan.

sentences.zh: 建中四年卒，年六十二，贈吏部尚書。

translations.literal: He died in the fourth year of Jianzhong at the age of sixty-two and was posthumously appointed Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourth year of the Jianzhong reign at the age of sixty-two and was posthumously appointed Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 韋倫，系本京兆。

translations.literal: Wei Lun traced his lineage to Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Lun traced his lineage to Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 父光乘，在開元、天寶間為朔方節度使。

translations.literal: His father Guangcheng served as military commissioner of Shuofang during the Kaiyuan and Tianbao reigns.
translations.idiomatic: His father Guangcheng served as military commissioner of Shuofang during the Kaiyuan and Tianbao reigns.

sentences.zh: 倫以蔭調藍田尉，幹力勤濟，楊國忠署為鑄錢內作使判官。

translations.literal: Lun entered service by yin privilege as assistant magistrate of Lantian. Capable and diligent, he was appointed by Yang Guozhong as aide to the Commissioner of Internal Minting.
translations.idiomatic: Lun entered service by yin privilege as assistant magistrate of Lantian. Capable and diligent, he was appointed by Yang Guozhong as aide to the Commissioner of Internal Minting.

sentences.zh: 國忠多發州縣齊人令鼓鑄，督非所習，雖箠失苛嚴，愈無功。

translations.literal: Guozhong frequently dispatched people from prefectures and counties who were alike in background to cast coins. They were supervised in work they had not mastered, and though beatings were lost in harsh severity, there was ever less success.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhong frequently dispatched ordinary people from prefectures and counties to cast coins. They were supervised in work they had not mastered, and though beatings grew ever harsher, there was ever less success.

sentences.zh: 倫請準直募匠，代無聊之人，繇是役用減，鼓鑄多矣。

translations.literal: Lun requested to recruit craftsmen at fair wages in place of idle and destitute people. Thereby corvée labor was reduced and coin casting greatly increased.
translations.idiomatic: Lun requested to recruit craftsmen at fair wages in place of idle and destitute people. Thereby corvée labor was reduced and coin casting greatly increased.

sentences.zh: 玄宗晚節盛營宮室，吏介以為欺，倫閱實工員，省費倍。

translations.literal: In his later years Emperor Xuanzong greatly built palaces. Minor officials used this to deceive. Lun verified the actual number of workers and reduced expenses by half.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years Emperor Xuanzong greatly built palaces. Minor officials used this to deceive. Lun verified the actual number of workers and reduced expenses by half.

sentences.zh: 從帝入蜀，以監察御史為劍南節度行軍司馬、置頓判官。

translations.literal: He followed the emperor into Shu and served as Censor, Acting Army Vice Commander of the Jiannan Military Commission and Aide for Encampment Arrangements.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the emperor into Shu and served as Censor, Acting Army Vice Commander of the Jiannan Military Commission and Aide for Encampment Arrangements.

sentences.zh: 時中人衛卒多侵暴，尤難治，倫以清儉自將，西人賴濟。

translations.literal: At that time eunuch guards and soldiers often committed aggression and were especially difficult to govern. Lun led himself with purity and frugality, and the people of the west relied on him for relief.
translations.idiomatic: At that time eunuch guards and soldiers often committed aggression and were especially difficult to govern. Lun led himself with purity and frugality, and the people of the west relied on him for relief.

sentences.zh: 中宦疾之，以讒貶衡州司戶參軍。

translations.literal: The eunuchs resented him and through slander had him demoted to Revenue Section Staff Assistant of Heng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuchs resented him and through slander had him demoted to Revenue Section Staff Assistant of Heng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 度支使第五琦薦倫才，擢商州刺史、荊襄道租庸使。

translations.literal: The Fiscal Commissioner Diwu Qi recommended Lun's talent, and he was promoted to prefect of Shang Prefecture and Corvée Commissioner of the Jingxiang Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: The Fiscal Commissioner Diwu Qi recommended Lun's talent, and he was promoted to prefect of Shang Prefecture and Corvée Commissioner of the Jingxiang Circuit.

sentences.zh: 襄州裨將康楚元亂，自稱東楚義王，刺史王政棄城遁。

translations.literal: Kang Chuyuan, a deputy general of Xiang Prefecture, rebelled and styled himself King of Righteousness of Eastern Chu. Prefect Wang Zheng abandoned the city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Kang Chuyuan, a deputy general of Xiang Prefecture, rebelled and styled himself King of Righteousness of Eastern Chu. Prefect Wang Zheng abandoned the city and fled.

sentences.zh: 賊南襲江陵，絕漢、沔餉道。

translations.literal: The rebels raided south to Jiangling and cut off the supply routes of the Han and Mian.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels raided south to Jiangling and cut off the supply routes of the Han and Mian.

sentences.zh: 倫調兵屯鄧州，厚撫降賊。

translations.literal: Lun deployed troops to encamp at Deng Prefecture and generously treated surrendered rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Lun deployed troops to encamp at Deng Prefecture and generously treated surrendered rebels.

sentences.zh: 寇益怠，乃擊禽楚元以獻，收租庸二百萬緡。

translations.literal: The bandits grew ever more lax, and he then struck and captured Chuyuan to present to the court, collecting 2,000,000 strings of corvée revenue.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits grew ever more lax, and he then struck and captured Chuyuan to present to the court, collecting 2,000,000 strings of corvée revenue.

sentences.zh: 召為衛尉卿，俄兼寧、隴二州刺史。

translations.literal: He was summoned to serve as Minister of the Guard and soon additionally held the posts of prefect of the two prefectures of Ning and Long.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to serve as Minister of the Guard and soon also served as prefect of Ning and Long.

sentences.zh: 乾元中，襄州亂，詔倫為山南東道節度使，而李輔國方恣橫，倫不肯謁，憾之，中罷為秦州刺史。

translations.literal: In the Qianyuan era, Xiang Prefecture was in disorder. An edict appointed Lun military commissioner of Shannan East Circuit, but Li Fuguo was then acting with unrestrained arrogance. Lun refused to pay him a visit, and Fuguo resented this and had him removed midway to serve as prefect of Qin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qianyuan era, when Xiang Prefecture fell into disorder, an edict appointed Lun military commissioner of Shannan East Circuit. Li Fuguo was then acting with unrestrained arrogance, and when Lun refused to pay him a visit, Fuguo resented it and had him removed to serve as prefect of Qin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃、党項歲入邊，倫兵寡，數格虜，敗，貶巴州長史，徙務川尉。

translations.literal: Tibetans and Tangut tribesmen raided the border year after year. Lun's troops were few. He repeatedly blocked the barbarians but was defeated, demoted to Senior Administrator of Ba Prefecture, and transferred to assistant magistrate of Wuchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Tibetans and Tangut tribesmen raided the border year after year. With too few troops, Lun repeatedly tried to block them but was defeated, demoted to Senior Administrator of Ba Prefecture, and transferred to assistant magistrate of Wuchuan.

sentences.zh: 代宗立，連拜忠、臺、饒三州刺史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Daizong ascended the throne, Lun was in succession appointed prefect of the three prefectures of Zhong, Tai, and Rao.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Daizong ascended the throne, Lun was appointed in succession to the prefectures of Zhong, Tai, and Rao.

sentences.zh: 宦者呂太一反嶺南，詔拜倫韶州刺史、韶連郴都團練使。

translations.literal: The eunuch Lü Taiyi rebelled in Lingnan. An edict appointed Lun prefect of Shao Prefecture and Commander-in-Chief of the Shao, Lian, and Chen Defense Command.
translations.idiomatic: When the eunuch Lü Taiyi rebelled in Lingnan, an edict appointed Lun prefect of Shao Prefecture and Commander-in-Chief of the Shao, Lian, and Chen Defense Command.

sentences.zh: 為太一反間，貶信州司馬，斥棄十年，客豫章。

translations.literal: Through Taiyi's counter-intrigue he was demoted to Vice Prefect of Xin Prefecture, cast aside for ten years, and lived as a guest in Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: Through Taiyi's counter-intrigue he was demoted to Vice Prefect of Xin Prefecture, cast aside for ten years, and lived as a guest in Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 德宗嗣位，選使絕域者，擢倫太常少卿，充和吐蕃使。

translations.literal: When Emperor Dezong succeeded to the throne, in selecting envoys to distant lands he promoted Lun to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and appointed him envoy for peace with Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Dezong succeeded to the throne, he promoted Lun to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and appointed him envoy for peace with Tibet.

sentences.zh: 倫至，諭天子威德，贊普順悅，乃入獻。

translations.literal: When Lun arrived, he expounded the Son of Heaven's authority and virtue. The zanpu was pleased and compliant and then entered to present tribute.
translations.idiomatic: When Lun arrived, he expounded the emperor's authority and virtue. The Tibetan ruler was pleased and compliant and then came to present tribute.

sentences.zh: 還，進太常卿，兼御史大夫。

translations.literal: On his return he was promoted to Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and additionally appointed Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was promoted to Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and additionally appointed Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 再使，如旨。

translations.literal: On a second mission, he fulfilled the imperial intent.
translations.idiomatic: On a second mission, he fulfilled the emperor's intent.

sentences.zh: 倫處朝，數論政得失，宰相盧杞惡之，改太子少保。

translations.literal: While serving at court, Lun repeatedly discussed the rights and wrongs of government. Chief Minister Lu Qi resented him and transferred him to Junior Mentor of the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: While serving at court, Lun repeatedly discussed the rights and wrongs of government. Chief Minister Lu Qi resented him and transferred him to Junior Mentor of the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 從狩奉天。

translations.literal: He followed the emperor on the hunt at Fengtian.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied the emperor when he fled to Fengtian.

sentences.zh: 及杞敗，關播罷為刑部尚書，倫在朝堂流涕曰：「宰相無狀，使天下至此，不失為尚書，後何勸？」

translations.literal: When Qi was defeated, Guan Bo was dismissed and made Minister of Justice. Lun wept in the court hall and said: "The chief minister was unworthy and brought the realm to this pass. Yet he is not even removed from being a minister—what encouragement is there hereafter?
translations.idiomatic: When Qi was defeated, Guan Bo was dismissed and made Minister of Justice. Lun wept in the court hall and said: "The chief minister was unworthy and brought the realm to this pass. Yet he is not even removed from being a minister—what encouragement is there hereafter?

sentences.zh: 聞者憚其公。

translations.literal: Those who heard this feared his impartiality.
translations.idiomatic: Those who heard this respected his impartiality.

sentences.zh: 帝後欲復用杞為刺史，倫苦諫，言懇至到，帝納之。

translations.literal: Later the emperor wished to reuse Qi as a prefect. Lun remonstrated bitterly with earnest and direct words, and the emperor accepted his advice.
translations.idiomatic: Later the emperor wished to reuse Qi as a prefect. Lun remonstrated bitterly with earnest and direct words, and the emperor accepted his advice.

sentences.zh: 進太子少師、郢國公，致仕。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Junior Preceptor of the Crown Prince and Duke of Ying, and retired from office.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Junior Preceptor of the Crown Prince and Duke of Ying, and retired from office.

sentences.zh: 時李楚琳以僕射兼衛尉卿，李忠誠以尚書兼少府監，倫言：「楚琳逆節，忠誠戎醜，不當寵以官。」

translations.literal: At that time Li Chulin held the post of Left Vice Director concurrently with Minister of the Guard, and Li Zhongcheng held the post of Minister concurrently with Director of the Palace Stores. Lun said: "Chulin is a rebel in conduct, and Zhongcheng is a barbarian villain—they ought not be favored with office.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Li Chulin held the post of Left Vice Director concurrently with Minister of the Guard, and Li Zhongcheng held the post of Minister concurrently with Director of the Palace Stores. Lun said: "Chulin is a rebel in conduct, and Zhongcheng is a barbarian villain—they ought not be favored with office.

sentences.zh: 又請為義倉，以捍無年；

translations.literal: He also requested the establishment of charity granaries to guard against years of famine;
translations.idiomatic: He also requested the establishment of charity granaries to guard against years of famine;

sentences.zh: 擇賢者，任帝左右。

translations.literal: to select worthy men and place them at the emperor's side.
translations.idiomatic: to select worthy men and place them at the emperor's side.

sentences.zh: 謂吐蕃豺虎野心，不可事信約，宜謹備邊。

translations.literal: He said that Tibet had the heart of wolves and tigers and could not be served with trust and treaties, and that the border ought to be carefully guarded.
translations.idiomatic: He said that Tibet had the heart of wolves and tigers and could not be trusted with treaties, and that the border ought to be carefully guarded.

sentences.zh: 帝善其言，厚禮之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved his words and treated him with generous courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved his words and treated him with generous courtesy.

sentences.zh: 居家以孝慈稱。

translations.literal: At home he was known for filial piety and kindness.
translations.idiomatic: At home he was known for filial piety and kindness.

sentences.zh: 卒，年八十三，贈揚州都督，謚曰肅。

translations.literal: He died at the age of eighty-three, was posthumously appointed Military Governor of Yang Prefecture, and was given the posthumous title Solemn.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of eighty-three, was posthumously appointed Military Governor of Yang Prefecture, and was given the posthumous title Solemn.

sentences.zh: 薛玨，字溫如，河中寶鼎人。

translations.literal: Xue Jue, styled Wenru, was a native of Baoding in Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Jue, courtesy name Wenru, was a native of Baoding in Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 以蔭為懿德太子廟令，累遷乾陵臺令。

translations.literal: He entered service by yin privilege as Director of the Temple of the Virtuous Crown Prince and was transferred through successive posts to Director of the Qianling Platform.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service by yin privilege as Director of the Temple of the Virtuous Crown Prince and rose through successive posts to Director of the Qianling Platform.

sentences.zh: 歲中以清白聞，課第一，改昭應令，人請立石紀德，玨固讓。

translations.literal: Within the year he was known for integrity, ranked first in assessment, and was transferred to magistrate of Zhaoying. The people requested that a stone stele be erected to record his virtue, but Jue firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: Within the year he was known for integrity, ranked first in assessment, and was transferred to magistrate of Zhaoying. The people requested that a stone stele be erected to record his virtue, but Jue firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 遷楚州刺史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to prefect of Chu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to prefect of Chu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 初，州有營田，宰相遙領使，而刺史得專達，俸及它給百餘萬，田官數百，歲以優得遷，別戶三千，備刺史廝役。

translations.literal: At first the prefecture had garrison fields. The chief minister held the commission remotely, while the prefect could report directly.
